full_judgment: 4. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement wherein he contended, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable in its present form and it was barred by limitation. He, however denied the case of the plaintiff and stated that he took the jote settlement from Jogendra Kumar Bhattacharjee about 20 years back at a monthly rental of Rs 1.50 per Kedar and since then he had been possessing the suit-land and that during the last survey and settlement operation, the record of rights stood wrongly in the name of the aforesaid Ex-landlord. The defendant No.1 having failed to get the record of right correctly and amicably recorded in his name in the Khatian, filed the Miscellaneous Case No.491 of 1969 and got an ex parte order in his favour for correction of the record of rights and accordingly, the Khatian was modified;. that there was no suppression of notices as alleged in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case; it was rather the plaintiff who in collusion with the lower rank staff of the Enemy Property Office, Sylhet filed this suit having no subsisting interest in the suit-land and as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed with cost.
